title: Edge Device Vendor Security Questionnaire (Template)
summary: Template questionnaire for assessing security posture of vendors providing edge devices or on-prem inference appliances. Focuses on firmware, supply chain, physical access, local telemetry, model artifact protection, and attestation procedures.
body:
Purpose:
This questionnaire is intended for procurement and security teams evaluating suppliers of edge inference devices, on-prem appliances, or partner-managed hardware used to run Redwood Inference model variants. The goal is to capture technical controls, product lifecycle practices, and operational assurances relevant to protecting model weights, data processed at the edge, and the integrity of telemetry that Redwood may rely on for billing/telemetry.

How to use this template:
- Send as part of initial security intake or RFP response.
- Ask vendors to attach evidence (architectural diagrams, firmware signing artifacts, attestation logs, test reports).
- Score responses using the attached scoring rubric (0 = no, 1 = partial, 2 = full).
- Request remediation plans for items scoring 0 or 1 before pilot approval.

Section A — Product & Deployment Overview
1) Product description: Provide a short summary of the device/appliance, supported OS/RTOS, and typical deployment topologies (air-gapped, NATed, cloud-connected).
2) Intended use-case: Is the device designed to perform local inference only, or also forward telemetry/aggregates to vendor or Redwood endpoints?
3) Model management: How are model binaries/weights delivered after procurement? (OTA, USB, signed container, pre-baked).
4) Supported compute stack: CPU/GPU/accelerator make and driver stack versions.

Section B — Firmware/Software Integrity
5) Firmware signing: Are firmware images cryptographically signed? Provide algorithm and signing authority process.
6) Secure boot: Does the device implement measured/verified secure boot to prevent unsigned code execution?
7) Runtime attestation: Does the device support runtime attestation (e.g., TPM/TEE attestation) to prove firmware and key material haven't been tampered with?
8) Update process: Describe the OTA update mechanism, rollback protection, and how updates are end-to-end authenticated.
9) Vulnerability disclosure & patching SLA: What are your out-of-band vulnerability reporting channels and patch timelines for critical/important vulnerabilities?

Section C — Key & Secret Management
10) Key storage: Where are model keys, signing keys, or device identity keys stored (TEE, TPM, secure element, filesystem encrypted)?
11) Root-of-trust lifecycle: Describe key generation, rotation cadence, and key destruction procedures at EOL or RMA.
12) Secret handling in logs: Are any secrets or private keys ever written to logs or telemetry? If yes, explain redaction controls.

Section D — Model Artifact Protection
13) Model encryption: Are model artifacts encrypted at rest on-device? State encryption algorithms and key provenance.
14) Access controls: How is access to model artifacts protected from local processes or users on the device?
15) Derivative protections: What restrictions or technical controls exist to prevent unauthorized copying or exfiltration of full model weights?

Section E — Data Handling & Telemetry
16) Local data processing: Describe which customer data may be persisted locally and retention defaults.
17) Telemetry collection: Enumerate telemetry categories sent to your service and default sampling/aggregation. Provide opt-out controls for telemetry.
18) Minimization and sampling: What mechanisms are in place to minimize collection of PII or prompt content? Is local filtering/pseudonymization supported before transmission?
19) Telemetry integrity: How do you ensure the authenticity and integrity of telemetry used for billing/usage? Are telemetry events signed/attested?

Section F — Network & Access Controls
20) Network segmentation: Describe how the device isolates inference workloads from administrative or management plane traffic.
21) Local network protections: Are there built-in host-based firewalls, port restrictions, or interface whitelists?
22) Remote access & support: What remote support mechanisms are available (SSH, vendor-agent, VPN)? How is support access gated and logged?
23) Authentication: Which authentication methods are supported for admin access (local password, certs, MFA, hardware tokens)?

Section G — Physical Security & Supply Chain
24) Tamper evidence and detection: Does hardware provide tamper-evident seals or tamper-detection sensors? Describe response behavior on tamper detection.
25) Component provenance: Provide summary of supply chain controls for critical components (trusted foundries, screening, chain of custody).
26) Secure manufacturing: Are keys provisioned at factory? If so, describe protection during provisioning and transport.
27) End-of-life and RMA: Describe secure wipe/crypto-erase processes for devices returned or decommissioned.

Section H — Logging, Forensics, & Audits
28) Local audit logs: What logs are stored on-device (commands, model loads, user authentication)? Retention policy?
29) Forensics readiness: Are readonly forensic images supported for incident response? How are they generated without altering evidence?
30) External auditability: Do you subject devices/firmware to independent security reviews or penetration tests? Provide reports or attestations if available.

Section I — Compliance, Privacy & Legal Controls
31) Data residency: Can you support on-prem or regional-only telemetry upload to meet data residency requirements?
32) DPA/processor controls: Are you willing to sign standard DPA terms and incorporate specific controls for inference data processed on-device?
33) Subprocessor disclosure: List third-party services that receive telemetry, analytics, or model telemetry data.
34) Insurance & liability: Provide summary of cyber insurance coverage relevant to device compromise and data breach.

Section J — Operational & Deployment Controls
35) Secure defaults: Does the device ship with secure default configuration (ports closed, admin password required change)?
36) Hardening guidance: Provide a baseline hardening guide (recommended kernel flags, sysctl, process isolation).
37) Scale & telemetry volume: Typical telemetry volume per device per day and highwater marks for CPU/GPU utilization that would trigger vendor alerts.
38) Support for attestation-based gating: Can you integrate attestation checks into Redwood-managed rollouts (e.g., only allow model activation when device attestation passes)?

Scoring rubric (sample):
- 2: Full control or strong evidence provided (e.g., signed firmware, TEE-backed key storage).
- 1: Partial control or compensating controls (e.g., encrypted filesystem but keys in software).
- 0: No control or concerning gaps.

Evidence checklist (ask vendor to attach):
- Firmware signing public keys and verification procedure
- Secure boot/UEFI policy and measurements
- Sample attestation log from test device
- OTA update manifests and signature examples
- Pen test or third-party firmware review (redacted if needed)
- Device data flow diagram showing telemetry endpoints and retention windows

Questions for procurement negotiators:
- Will the vendor accept contract clauses requiring quarterly attestation reports and on-demand evidence for incidents?
- Can telemetry used for billing include cryptographic proof of origin (signed counters)?
- Is the vendor willing to attest on chain-of-custody for device provisioning and key injection?

Notes to reviewer:
- Items 5–9, 10–12, 13–15 are high risk for model & key protection—require score >=1 for pilot approval.
- Telemetry integrity (16–19, 29) is critical where Redwood depends on remote usage reporting. Consider mandating signed counters for billing.
- If vendor ships devices pre-loaded with model artifacts, require dual controls: encrypted model storage and attestation before activation.

Revision history:
- 2024-02-12 initial draft by Priya Sharma (security intake team).
- 2024-03-05 added scoring rubric, procurement negotiation prompts, and evidence checklist.

End of questionnaire template.
